I: this file is the source; those artifacts stay generated by packages/elements/scripts/build-surfaces.mjs and are sealed by the surfaces-sync gate). Package names and descriptions are read from each package.json at generation time, and every entryPoints[].name is verified against the package's src/index.ts exports, so a renamed or removed export fails the build instead of drifting.
intro: Above the components sits Kimen's GenUI layer: agents emit JSON UI specs
(data, never code), the neutral catalog validates them against the
published component surface, and the guarded renderer turns accepted
specs into DOM. Protocol adapters translate external vocabularies into
that neutral core and are disposable by design; the catalog and the
ki-* elements are the durable assets. These packages live in this

packages.whenToUse: Any boundary where agent-emitted JSON must become Kimen UI: validate specs standalone, render them with the guardrail enforced, stream them progressively, or keep a long-lived surface current with id-addressed batches. Both protocol adapters and any custom transport build on it.
packages.whenNotToUse: Hand-authored pages that never render agent output — use @kimen/elements directly.

entryPoints.name: validateUiSpec
entryPoints.summary: Accepts or rejects an agent-emitted UI spec against the catalog in use — the built-in generated catalog, or a registered one passed as options.catalog — before anything renders. The report lists every issue with a code (unknown-component, unknown-prop, invalid-prop-type, missing-required-prop, prop-out-of-range, unknown-slot, undeclared-action, invalid-child, action-not-allowed, url-scheme, url-origin, invalid-id, duplicate-id, forbidden-key, size-budget, depth-budget, malformed-spec), a path into the spec document and the offending value.

entryPoints.name: renderUiSpec
entryPoints.summary: Validates and renders a spec into options.surface through the guarded renderer: only components of the catalog in use render (options.catalog selects it; absent, the built-in catalog applies) plus the native primitives it carries, only actions declared in the spec dispatch (delivered as data to options.onAction), unknown props are rejected and no code path executes from spec data. Failures come back as diagnostics naming rule, path and value; nothing attaches on failure.

entryPoints.name: preflightUiSpec
entryPoints.summary: The guarded renderer's verdict without a DOM: runs exactly the preparation renderUiSpec runs before its first attach (purity wall, version gate, payload budget, catalog validation, then the depth, node-count, tag, activation and prop-name guards) and renders nothing. Use it at a DOM-less boundary — an MCP server, a service that checks specs before forwarding them — so that "valid" means "the renderer will paint it"; validateUiSpec alone accepts specs the renderer's tighter budgets refuse.

entryPoints.name: createStreamingRenderer
entryPoints.summary: Progressive rendering over a streamed spec: each push(node) validates one top-level subtree and attaches it only when fully valid; an invalid node fails closed while previously attached content remains, and the render budgets bind the accumulated stream. The catalog in use is fixed at creation via options.catalog.

entryPoints.name: createLiveSurface
entryPoints.summary: A long-lived surface changed through atomic batches of insert, set, text, remove and replace ops addressed by stable node ids: apply(batch) validates the whole batch and the state it would produce (purity wall, per-batch budgets, optional ifRevision, catalog, guards, state budgets) before any DOM write, rejects it whole with diagnostics while the surface stays live, and otherwise touches only the attributes, text and subtrees it names so focus, typed values and scroll survive. No set, replace or remove overwrites or discards checked/value/open the user changed unless forced and allowed by the host. Action events carry id, current path, revision and live data; snapshot() returns deep-frozen plain data.

entryPoints.name: createCatalog
entryPoints.summary: Registers your own components behind a data-only JSON facade — the exact entry shape of the generated catalog (tag, usage guidance, typed prop constraints, slots, events) — and returns a deeply frozen catalog that validateUiSpec and both renderers accept via options.catalog. The definition is untrusted input: it crosses the same purity wall as UI specs, tags must be conservative custom-element names, collisions with the extended catalog fail closed, usage guidance is mandatory, and every rejection is a RegistrationIssue naming code, path and offender. Pass { extend: catalogData } to compose with the built-in components, or omit it for a standalone catalog.

entryPoints.name: DEFAULT_RENDER_BUDGETS
entryPoints.summary: The declared render budgets (maxDepth 32, maxNodes 512, maxBytes 262144). A spec exactly at a budget passes; one beyond it is rejected before any node attaches. Hosts may tighten them via options.budgets; the renderer never renders past them. Standalone validation has its own ceilings, VALIDATION_MAX_BYTES (262144 UTF-8 bytes, overridable per call with maxBytes) and VALIDATION_MAX_DEPTH (256).

entryPoints.name: catalogData
entryPoints.summary: The generated catalog document itself: one entry per opted-in ki-* element and per native primitive with typed props, events, slots and when-to-use guidance, plus the elements version it derives from. Its schema version is exported as CATALOG_SCHEMA_VERSION.

entryPoints.name: NATIVE_PRIMITIVE_TAGS
entryPoints.summary: The closed set of native HTML elements a spec may carry next to catalog components: h2, h3, h4, p, strong and em for text, img for images and div for layout. They take the host page's typography, carry only their declared attributes (img: src under the URL policy, alt that is a description or exactly empty for decoration, width, height; div: direction, gap on the --ki-space-* steps, align, justify, wrap), never bind an action, and lay out through the CSSOM so a CSP without unsafe-inline styles holds. They come with the built-in catalog and with catalogs that extend it; a consumer definition can never declare one.

packages.whenToUse: Configure ANY LLM to emit valid Kimen UI specs: derive a system prompt, a catalog-specialized JSON Schema (with provider-strict lowerings) or a tool definition from the catalog in use — built-in or registered — and close the reliability loop with normalization and a single-round repair message.
packages.whenNotToUse: Enforcement: the artifacts are advisory. Validation and rendering stay in @kimen/catalog; hosts that already emit valid specs need nothing from this package.

entryPoints.name: catalogPrompt
entryPoints.summary: Model-facing prompt: format rules, every component's when-to-use and when-NOT-to-use guidance verbatim, props with enums inline, and one example spec that validates against the same catalog. The universal fallback — works with any model, no structured-output support required.

entryPoints.name: uiSpecJsonSchema
entryPoints.summary: The neutral UI-spec format specialized to the catalog as a JSON Schema document: one branch per component, closed props and enums, closed objects everywhere. Targets: draft-2020-12 (default) and openai-strict (all-required closed objects, recursion via $ref, only the keywords the provider documents, its published limits enforced with named offenders). Deterministic and version-stamped; fail-closed on skew, bad subsets and exceeded limits — never a silent truncation.

entryPoints.name: uiSpecTool
entryPoints.summary: Provider-neutral tool definition { name: 'emit_ui', description, inputSchema } wrapping exactly the lowered schema for the same options; maps mechanically onto any provider's tool or function surface.

entryPoints.name: normalizeEmission
entryPoints.summary: Strips the placeholders strict-mode all-required schemas force a model to emit (null-valued props, null action bindings, empty props containers) and touches nothing else. Pure cleanup over a fresh clone; output is untrusted until validateUiSpec passes.

entryPoints.name: repairPrompt
entryPoints.summary: Formats a failed ValidationReport into ONE corrective message naming every issue's code, path and offender, or null when the report is ok. The single-round-then-fail-closed policy is fixed.

packages.whenToUse: Your agent runtime speaks the A2UI protocol and its surfaces should render as Kimen components with the guardrail enforced.
packages.whenNotToUse: The agent can emit neutral Kimen UI specs directly (use @kimen/catalog alone), or the host is an MCP Apps client (use @kimen/adapter-mcp-apps).

entryPoints.name: createA2uiAdapter
entryPoints.summary: Creates the translation boundary: adapter.apply(message) turns A2UI 1.0 and v0.9.1 messages (createSurface, updateComponents, updateDataModel, deleteSurface) into neutral UI specs rendered only through the guarded renderer, resolving the surface data model inside the adapter. Each message is validated against the version its envelope declares, and a surface accepts only the version that created it. User interactions return through options.onAction as A2UI action events in the surface's version, rejected messages through options.onError as VALIDATION_FAILED errors; unmapped basic-catalog types degrade to a fixed fallback reported through options.onDegradation, and every A2UI 1.0 callRendererFunction is refused through options.onFunctionResponse.

entryPoints.name: SUPPORTED_A2UI_VERSIONS
entryPoints.summary: The exact A2UI envelope versions this adapter accepts: 1.0 (preferred) plus v0.9.1 and v0.9 (one payload-compatible family), each pinned to an upstream commit in A2UI_PROTOCOLS and versioned with the adapter in COMPAT.md.

entryPoints.name: A2UI_COVERAGE
entryPoints.summary: Machine-readable coverage table declaring how each A2UI 0.9.1 basic-catalog component type is handled: mapped to catalog components, rendered inline, degraded as unmapped, or forbidden. A2UI_V1_COVERAGE is the A2UI 1.0 counterpart.

entryPoints.name: A2UI_RENDERER_CAPABILITIES
entryPoints.summary: The renderer capabilities a host transport attaches for each supported A2UI version, preferred version (1.0) first: the metadata key (a2uiRendererCapabilities or a2uiClientCapabilities) and its value naming the basic catalog of that version.

packages.whenToUse: You ship an MCP server and want tool results to render as interactive Kimen surfaces in MCP Apps (SEP-1865) hosts.
packages.whenNotToUse: The host is not an MCP Apps client, or you control the rendering surface directly — render neutral specs with @kimen/catalog instead.

entryPoints.name: declareToolSurface
entryPoints.summary: Declares in an MCP tool's _meta that its results render in a predeclared ui:// surface.

entryPoints.name: createKimenSurfaceResource
entryPoints.summary: The self-contained ui:// resource the server serves: one HTML document with every script and style inline, a no-network content policy, and the guarded renderer as its only render path.

entryPoints.name: surfaceToolResult
entryPoints.summary: Wraps a neutral UI spec plus a plain-text fallback as an MCP CallToolResult (spec in structuredContent.kimenSurface, text in content), so hosts without interactive surfaces still get text. The optional update { baseRevision, batch } is a live batch computed on the revision an action call carried: the surface applies it, keeping what the person is typing, only on that revision and when the live surface accepts it, and otherwise paints the full spec.

entryPoints.name: declareActionTool
entryPoints.summary: The app-only MCP tool (kimen_surface_action, _meta.ui.visibility ["app"]) that receives the surface's declared actions as tools/call { action, data, revision, id? } (the page revision the person acted on and the bound node's id; both optional in its schema); register it on the same server and validate the action.

entryPoints.name: acknowledgeSurfaceAction
entryPoints.summary: The action tool's answer for an action your server accepts. With { relay: true } the surface relays that exact action to the model as one ui/message, if the host advertises text messages: one line, kimen-surface-action followed by { action, data } as escaped JSON, at most 8192 bytes, built by the surface from what it sent, never from this result. Relay when the person's choice needs the model; leave it off for UI-only actions such as a refresh.

entryPoints.name: createSurfaceBridge
entryPoints.summary: Runs inside the surface document and speaks the MCP Apps 2026-01-26 lifecycle: sends ui/initialize, refuses an undeclared negotiated version, renders ui/notifications/tool-result specs through the guarded renderer and its live surface only after the handshake (applying a result's update when it was computed on the current page revision), answers ui/resource-teardown and ping, and dispatches only declared actions as tools/call; when the server acknowledges one for relay and the host advertises text messages, relays it once as ui/message. Non-protocol messages are ignored with no state change.

entryPoints.name: MCP_APPS_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS
entryPoints.summary: The exact MCP Apps protocol revisions this adapter supports, versioned with the adapter in COMPAT.md.
